guideTitle: 6 Best Bluetooth Trackers for Luggage in 2026
metaDescription: Six Bluetooth luggage trackers for iPhone and Android, compared on airline sharing, battery life, sound and water rating so a lost bag is easier to trace.
introParagraphs: A bag that does not come down the carousel is the moment a luggage tracker earns its place. Slip one in a suitcase and you can check on your phone whether it is still at the departure airport, on a truck or sitting in the wrong city. That view comes from the same crowd network that finds keys, so the tag only helps if it matches your phone.

We evaluated six trackers based on product specs and buyer feedback, with travel in mind: how long the battery lasts between trips, how loud the tag rings in a baggage hall, how it handles rain on a tarmac, and whether it can be shared with an airline or a travel partner. Two work with iPhone only, one is Android only, one works with Find My or Find Hub, one is Apple's AirTag and one is a slim tag that slides into a luggage sleeve.
Read the compatibility notes first, then use the packing tables to decide how many tags you need.

products.name: Apple AirTag (2nd Generation)
products.description:
The second generation AirTag is the luggage tag with the clearest travel feature. You can share its location temporarily and securely with trusted contacts, third parties or over 50 airline partners if a bag goes missing. That sharing is built into Find My, so there is nothing extra to install.

Upgraded Ultra Wideband and Bluetooth chips let you ping it from farther away, and a speaker that Apple says is 50% louder helps in a noisy baggage hall. Precision Finding gives step by step directions on iPhone and Apple Watch. The tradeoff is that it only works with Apple devices, and the listing gives no battery type or water rating.

It sells as a single and a 4-pack, and a bare tag needs a holder to attach to a bag handle. Compared with the ATUVOS iOS set at up to 100 dB it gives you airline sharing and arrows, while the ATUVOS gives more tags per box. Next to the Replglee set it is iPhone only but far deeper on iPhone.
products.bestFor: iPhone and Apple Watch travelers who want to share a bag location with an airline.

products.description:
The Replglee 4-pack is the travel pick for groups that mix iPhone and Android. The listing says it works with Google's Find Hub or Apple Find My, with Android 9 and above supported, and it states it is not for GPS or Huawei phones. The built-in speaker rings up to 110 dB, which is loud enough to hear in a packed suitcase.

Battery life is listed as up to 2 years, and the IP66 rating protects against rain and splashes on a wet tarmac. Cases come in the box, which is handy for attaching to straps. The tradeoff is that the brand is less established and each tag still joins only one network at a time.

Four tags cover two suitcases, a carry-on and a backpack. At 110 dB it is louder than the Vodyfu at 85 dB, and unlike the Vodyfu it also works on iPhone, though it gives no airline sharing like the Apple AirTag.

products.name: Vodyfu Air Tags 4 Pack for Android
products.description:
The Vodyfu 4-pack is a plain Android luggage tag set with a Google Find Hub connection. The listing says it is for Android only, not for iOS or GPS use, and that location data is encrypted with the help of Google's technology. A built-in speaker reaches up to 85 dB.

Battery life is listed as up to 2 years on Android, and the IP65 rating covers rain and splashes. That is a step below the IP66 on the Replglee set. The tradeoff is that it will not work with any iPhone, so a spouse with an iPhone cannot use it.

Four tags cover a pair of suitcases, a carry-on and a bag. At 85 dB it rings softer than the Replglee at 110 dB, but for Android-only households it keeps things simple with one network and no pairing choice. Next to the Apple AirTag it has no airline sharing, so you rely on Find Hub's own location view.

products.name: ATUVOS Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack (iOS)
products.description:
The ATUVOS iOS 4-pack is a straightforward luggage tag set for iPhone owners. The listing says the built-in speaker rings between 80 and 100 decibels, and you can ask Siri to ring it. Within about 200 feet you can use the Find My app to play a sound and see the position, and beyond that the Find My network does the work.

The listing stresses that only you can see where the tags are, because the location data is encrypted. There are no monthly or annual fees. Pairing goes through the Items tab and Add Item in Find My. The tradeoff is iPhone only compatibility and no stated battery type, water rating or airline sharing.

Four tags cover a family's bags in one box. Against the Apple AirTag it has no airline sharing but gives more tags per pack, and next to the UGREEN FineTrack 4-pack at up to 2 years it lists no battery life at all. For Android travelers, the Vodyfu is the safer fit.

products.badge: Best Slim Tag for Luggage Sleeves
products.name: Life360 Tile Slim
products.description:
The Tile Slim is the pick for travel documents and luggage tags because it is the thinnest Tile tracker. The listing says it slides into wallets, passports and luggage, so it works in a passport pouch or behind a luggage tag sleeve. It works on both iPhone and Android through the free Tile app.

You can press the tag to ring your phone even when the phone is silenced, which helps on a plane after a long day. A discreet SOS alert can notify loved ones if you feel unsafe, and tags can be added to the Life360 map for a family view. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no battery type, ring volume or water rating.

It runs on Tile's own network, not Apple Find My or Google Find Hub. Compared with the Replglee set at 110 dB it states no loudness, and unlike the Apple AirTag it has no airline sharing. It suits a traveler who wants one flat tag for documents.

products.name: UGREEN FineTrack Air Tracker Tags 4 Pack
products.description:
The UGREEN FineTrack 4-pack is the iPhone luggage set for people who want to forget about batteries for a while. The listing claims a replaceable battery that lasts up to 2 years, compared with 1 year for standard trackers, and you can check each tag's battery level in the app. It is Apple MFi certified and pairs in one tap.

When a tag moves out of range, Find My sends a lost alert with the last known location, and Lost Mode lets you add contact details. The listing also calls it child-safe certified. The tradeoff is iPhone only compatibility, and the listing gives no ring volume or water rating.

Four tags cover a family's checked bags and carry-ons. It lists a longer battery than the ATUVOS, which states none, but has no airline sharing like the Apple AirTag, and next to the Replglee it covers only iPhone while the Replglee adds Android and a 110 dB alarm.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A luggage tag is useless if it cannot talk to your phone. The Apple AirTag (2nd Generation), ATUVOS iOS set and UGREEN FineTrack are iPhone only, the Vodyfu is Android only, and the Replglee works with Google Find Hub or Apple Find My. The Life360 Tile Slim runs on Tile's own network for both phone types. A tag joins one network at a time, so if two travelers use different phones, buy a pack and pair each tag to its owner.

When a bag is lost, the airline needs to see where it is. The Apple AirTag can share location with over 50 airline partners, which is a real convenience for iPhone owners. None of the other picks here list that feature, so you would share a screenshot or a link instead. Find My also lets you share a tag with other people. If you fly often with checked bags, favor the tag with a stated airline option.

A dead tag is a lost bag in waiting, so battery life matters more than for keys. The UGREEN FineTrack, Replglee and Vodyfu all list up to 2 years, while the ATUVOS and Tile Slim listings state no duration. Check the battery level in the app before a trip, and replace a coin cell the week before you fly. Do not trust a tag that has sat in a suitcase for years.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Alarm loud enough for a hall
buyingCriteria.explanation: Baggage halls are noisy, so a quiet beep is easy to miss. The Replglee lists up to 110 dB, the ATUVOS 80 to 100 dB, the Vodyfu up to 85 dB, and the Apple AirTag has a speaker 50% louder than before. The Tile Slim listing gives no figure. Decibel numbers are manufacturer claims, so treat them as rough. A louder ring helps when the bag is in a pile of identical cases.

Luggage rides on wet ramps and gets tossed, so the tag should survive. The Replglee lists IP66, the Vodyfu IP65, and the UGREEN FineTrack, ATUVOS, Apple AirTag and Tile Slim state no rating. IP65 and IP66 protect against jets of water, not full submersion. Tuck the tag inside the bag or in an internal pocket, not on an exposed handle. That alone protects it better than any rating.

Where the tag sits changes what you need. A flat tag such as the Tile Slim slides into a luggage sleeve or passport pouch, while a round disc fits an inner pocket. The bare Apple AirTag needs a holder to attach to a handle. A tag hidden inside a bag is harder for a thief or handler to remove. Place one in each checked bag and one in your carry-on.

howWeEvaluated.title: Travel-specific features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for features that help when a bag goes missing. The Apple AirTag (2nd Generation) can share location with over 50 airline partners, while the Tile Slim adds a discreet SOS alert and a Life360 map. Picks without a travel-specific feature were judged on the basics.

howWeEvaluated.title: Network and phone support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which phones each tag works with. The Replglee supports Find Hub or Find My, the Vodyfu is Android only, and the AirTag, ATUVOS and UGREEN FineTrack are iPhone only. Clear compatibility counted for more than extra features.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and alarm
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated battery life and alarm volume. The Replglee, Vodyfu and UGREEN FineTrack list up to 2 years, and the Replglee reaches up to 110 dB, the ATUVOS 80 to 100 dB and the Vodyfu 85 dB. Where a listing was silent, as with the Tile Slim, we did not assume a figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Durability and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed stated water ratings and how the tag attaches. The Replglee lists IP66 and the Vodyfu IP65, while the Tile Slim is the flat option for documents. A published rating counted more than a general claim of toughness.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each pick by what it does best, not by price or popularity. The AirTag leads on airline sharing, the Replglee on dual-network volume, the Vodyfu on Android simplicity, the ATUVOS on iPhone four-packs, the Tile Slim on thin documents and the UGREEN FineTrack on stated battery. We did not rank on popularity or review counts.

faq.q: Where should I put a tracker in my suitcase?
faq.a: Place it inside an interior pocket or sewn lining, not on an exposed handle or outer pocket. A hidden tag is harder for a handler or thief to spot and remove. Leave the tag away from large metal items, which can block signal. Avoid sealing it inside thick metal or foil-lined pouches.

faq.q: Which tag is best for iPhone travelers?
faq.a: The Apple AirTag (2nd Generation) is the strongest iPhone pick because it can share location with over 50 airline partners and offers Precision Finding. If you want four tags in a box, the UGREEN FineTrack lists up to 2 years of battery and the ATUVOS lists 80 to 100 dB.

faq.q: Can I use an Android tag and an iPhone together?
faq.a: Not on the same tag. The Replglee lets you pick Google Find Hub or Apple Find My at setup, but each tag joins only one network. In a mixed travel party, pair each tag to the phone of the person who owns that bag.

faq.q: Will a tracker show live bag location during a flight?
faq.a: No, and this is the most common misconception. These tags use Bluetooth and rely on nearby phones in the network to report a last known location. If no compatible phone is nearby, the location can be stale until one passes.

faq.q: How often should I change the battery?
faq.a: Check the level in the app before every trip. The UGREEN FineTrack, Replglee and Vodyfu list up to 2 years, but real life depends on use. Replace a coin cell the week before a long trip so you are not relying on an old one.

faq.q: Should I put a tracker in every bag?
faq.a: Yes, one tag per bag is the simplest rule. A carry-on and a checked suitcase each need their own tag, and a four-pack covers a small family. Pair each tag clearly in the app and name it after the bag so you can tell them apart at a glance.
